text:
Maria Santos: Quick update — I ran a block-manager block-size / reuse / compaction sweep for paged-attn on the 8k-seq benchmark (A100,x2). High level: found tradeoffs between compaction cost and fragmentation; also ran experiments with eager-free + buffer reuse and a small allocator tweak. Posting short notes + numbers, asking for suggestions before I open a PR.

Maria Santos: TL;DR:
- 64KB blocks: low compaction CPU work but high fragmentation -> ~12% higher peak memory vs baseline
- 128KB blocks: best balance on our traces, peak mem down ~9%, compaction spikes modest
- 256KB blocks: lowest fragmentation but when compaction runs it stalls streaming and increases p99 latency by ~18%
- Eager-free + reuse (reuse window=2s): peak mem -14%, but observed extra kernel launches (~+6%) and small throughput jitter
- Post-kernsel-change regression: A100 regressed ~6% throughput in long-tail requests when using 256KB blocks

Anand Patel: Can you paste the profiling snippets? GPU timeline + block-manager counters (alloc/free/compactions) would help.

Maria Santos: Pasting minimal profiling snippets:
```
# simplified counters aggregated over 30m run
blocks_allocated: 12.3k
blocks_reused: 8.9k
compaction_runs: 142
avg_compact_time_ms: 23.4 (256KB), 12.1 (128KB), 6.8 (64KB)
peak_gpu_mem_gb: 94.1 (64K), 85.6 (128K), 82.9 (256K)
p99_latency_ms: 210 (256K), 178 (128K), 164 (64K)
```
Notes: compaction time dominated by copying live fragments; copy bandwidth plateau on A100 when compaction concurrent with attention kernel.

Kevin Liu: Hmm — the p99 increase with 256KB looks like compaction + kernel scheduling collision. Did the kernel-selection change introduce extra memcpy or temp buffers? I remember a recent fallback that materializes a contiguous KV buffer for some kernels.

Maria Santos: Yes, good catch. After the kernel-selection update, some attention kernels prefer contiguous KV and we added a transient copy path when block layout isn't contiguous. For 256KB blocks that copy cost is large because each compaction run touches a bigger contiguous region.

Olga Smirnova: CI perf flagged the regression on the nightly long-run suite. Failing test: `paged-attn-8k-longrun` (throughput -5.9%, p99 +11%). I can attach the flame graphs if useful.

ci-bot: Run 2026-03-16-02: paged-attn-8k-longrun: baseline=156k tokens/s, current=146.8k tokens/s, delta=-5.9%. Artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/paged-attn/2026-03-16/longrun/{flame.svg,trace.json}

Devon Park: Two actionable experiments to try in parallel: (1) reduce compaction frequency threshold (compact when free<10% vs current <20%), (2) enable partial compaction that only compacts cold regions (marks hot blocks with a bit). Also try toggling the contiguous-copy fallback to be size-aware (disable for blocks >128KB).

Anand Patel: I ran a micro-experiment with partial compaction + size-aware-copy disabled for >128KB blocks. Results on dev cluster: peak mem about same as 128KB baseline, throughput improved ~3%, p99 down ~6%. Command I used: 
```
./bin/paged-attn-run --seq 8192 --blocks 128k --compaction-threshold 0.1 --partial-compact=true --contig-copy-max=131072 
```
Logs: compaction_runs dropped 60%, avg_compact_time_ms stayed ~13ms, blocks_reused up 12%.

Kevin Liu: Sounds promising. My worry: partial compaction adds bookkeeping overhead. Did you measure CPU overhead (scheduler thread)?

Anand Patel: CPU overhead minimal in the dev run (scheduler cpu +2%), most savings on the GPU side. The bookkeeping is just a small bitmap and an age counter per block.

Maria Santos: Next steps I'm proposing:
- Default block size -> 128KB for paged-attn in container images for now
- Enable partial compaction + compaction-threshold=0.1 behind feature flag (runtime flag `RW_PAGED_PARTIAL_COMPACT=1`)
- Contiguous-copy fallback: make it size-aware (max copy size 128KB) and add a fast-path that merges only when contiguous regions >2 blocks
- Add a perf test to nightly that runs the longrun with 8k seq and asserts throughput within -3% of baseline

Olga Smirnova: +1 on the feature-flag rollout. I'll triage the failing CI test to track progress.

Devon Park: For the allocator tweak I also suggest adding a small workspace pre-reserve (8% overhead) to reduce transient compactions during bursts. We should test with stress traces to verify it doesn't blow peak mem.

Maria Santos: I'll run the two combined configs (128KB blocks + partial compaction + pre-reserve 8%) on staging and post results here by EOD. If numbers look good I'll open a PR with the runtime flags and a short design note.

Kevin Liu: One more ask — please capture nvprof traces when compaction runs concurrently with attention kernels. We need to verify whether the stall is memcpy-bound or kernel-sync-bound.

Maria Santos: Will do. Thanks all.

Anand Patel: Happy to help run more sweeps and look at the traces.

ci-bot: Note: nightly perf alert created (#perf-2026-03-16-176945) referencing this thread.

Maria Santos: OK creating the staging runs now, will update with numbers. :thumbsup:
